Collective Worship
Collective worship is a valued and statutory part of school life in every school in England. All maintained schools are required to provide a daily act of collective worship for all pupils, in accordance with the School Standards and Framework Act 1998.
At St Matthew’s C of E Primary School, collective worship is at the heart of our daily life; it is inclusive, invitational and inspiring and reflects our Christian vision: “Let your light shine” (Matthew 5:16).
Collective worship is viewed as a cherished time when our whole school community comes together to reflect, pray, and grow spiritually. Rooted in our Christian foundation, it plays a central role in nurturing the flourishing of every child and adult, supporting them to live well together and shine as individuals.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Matthew's CofE Primary School - Our Vision
pageCache.text:
Our Vision
St Matthew's Theologically Rooted Vision
At St Matthew’s, our vision is to ‘Let your light shine’. We draw our spirituality from our awareness that: God said, “Let there be light”; that Jesus came as the light of the world; and that he calls us to live with him in Heaven – a place where there is no darkness. Guided by our Christian values, we nurture a community where every child is encouraged to be brave, respectful, inspirational, grateful, honest and to shine together. As a rights-respecting school, we are dedicated to creating a safe and inclusive environment where every child can flourish. We support our pupils in becoming loving, confident, resilient and successful global citizens, driven to make a difference, serving our school community and beyond. Our commitment to high aspirations, underpinned by mutual respect and support, ensures that every child is known, valued and empowered to reach their full potential - shining brightly in all they do.
Our School Motto
Our school motto, ‘Together we let our light shine bright’, is taken from and inspired by Jesus' Sermon on the Mount from St Matthew’s Gospel 5:16 and embodies our Christian ethos.
It is a clear and powerful reminder for all our children and staff to use the unique and special gifts that God has given us, to make a positive difference to others, to work together for goodness, and most importantly, to reflect Jesus and God’s love in all we do – shining as a beacon of hope within our community and in the wider world.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Matthew's CofE Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to St Matthew’s Church of England Primary School.
We are a happy, welcoming one-form entry school where children of all faiths and backgrounds are nurtured to grow, thrive, and live out our motto: 'Together we let our light shine bright'. As a small and diverse school family, inclusion and belonging sit at the heart of everything we do. Every child is truly known, valued, and encouraged to shine in their own unique way.
Our BRIGHT values—Brave, Respectful, Inspirational, Grateful, Honest, and Together—guide our daily life and shape the kind of community we aspire to be. We want our pupils to be brave in their learning, respectful in their relationships, grateful for the opportunities they receive, honest in their actions, inspired and inspiring in equal measure, and united together as a caring and compassionate community.
As a Rights Respecting School, we are committed to nurturing confident, thoughtful, and compassionate learners who flourish academically, socially, and spiritually. We teach our children to understand their own rights and the rights of others, helping them to become empathetic young citizens who are ready to make a positive difference in the world.
Our rich and exciting curriculum reflects and serves the needs of our children and the community in which they are geographically and culturally rooted. Through high-quality teaching and a holistic approach to learning, we ignite curiosity and a passion for lifelong learning. We support children to discover their individual gifts and talents, develop a strong sense of self, become independent thinkers, and build the skills they need to thrive both now and in their future lives.
Community matters deeply to us. We value our partnerships with parents and carers and encourage them to be actively involved in their children’s education. By working closely together, we ensure that every child receives the best possible start to their learning journey. Our collaboration with families, our church, and the wider community strengthens the sense of belonging that makes St Matthew’s such a special place to grow and learn.
It is a joy and a privilege to lead such a vibrant and nurturing school family, where everyone's light shines brightly every day. I warmly invite you to explore our website and discover more about the values, relationships, and experiences that make St Matthew’s Primary School a place where every child can flourish.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Matthew's CofE Primary School - Breakfast & After School Clubs
pageCache.text:
Breakfast & After School Clubs
At St Matthew's, we are delighted to offer both a Breakfast and After School Club, designed to help parents balance work and family commitments.
Our Breakfast Club runs from 7.30am till the start of the school day. Once the registration form is completed, this can be used on an "as and when" basis. All children attending will receive breakfast (toast, cereal, crumpets, muffin etc). The cost of this is £2 per day for childcare and must be paid using ParentPay.
Every pupil is invited to join us for our free Breakfast Club from 8.15am every day.
We also have an After School Club which runs from the end of the school day up until 6pm. A registration form must be completed prior to your child's first time at this service – then it can be used on a regular basis or whenever it is needed. The cost of this is £7 per day and must be paid in advance using ParentPay.
Children attending After School Club receive a snack (noodles, fish fingers, hot dog etc), a piece of fruit and a drink and have a range of activities and games to participate in.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Matthew's CofE Primary School - Our Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum
Our curriculum is designed to provide a broad, balanced, and ambitious education that nurtures every child’s academic, personal, and spiritual development. Rooted in our Christian vision for every child to ‘Let your light shine’ (Matthew 5:16), and guided by our BRIGHT values - Bravery, Respect, Inspiration, Gratitude, Honesty, and Togetherness, we aim to equip all pupils with the knowledge, skills, and character to thrive in an ever-changing world.
Through engaging and inclusive learning experiences across all subjects of the National Curriculum, we aim to inspire curiosity, creativity, and a love of learning. Our learning is carefully sequenced so that children build secure knowledge and skills progressively over time. We help pupils make meaningful connections between their learning and the wider world, enabling them to understand its purpose, relevance to their lives and how it supports their future.
As a Rights Respecting School, children learn about their rights and responsibilities, which are woven throughout the curriculum and reflected in everyday school life. Our curriculum also celebrates the cultural diversity of our school community, helping children to develop respect, empathy and understanding for one another.
Children learn about the Global Goals, encouraging them to think critically about fairness, sustainability and their role in creating a better future. We aim to empower pupils to become positive ‘change-makers’ within their local community and beyond, understanding that even small actions can make a meaningful difference.
Oracy is key in our curriculum. We encourage children to speak confidently, articulate their ideas clearly in full sentences, explain their thinking and listen respectfully to others. Opportunities for discussion, questioning and purposeful talk are woven throughout all areas of learning, helping pupils to become effective communicators.
At St Matthew’s, we are committed to nurturing the holistic development of every child, supporting academic achievement alongside personal, social, spiritual and emotional growth. Through enriching and inspiring learning experiences and opportunities beyond the classroom, we broaden children's horizons, build confidence and develop character.
Our ambition is for every child to leave St Matthew’s, ready for the next stage of their education, as resilient, compassionate, capable young people, with a deep sense of responsibility to make a positive difference to others and our planet – letting their light shine brightly in the world.

pageCache.text:
Pupil Leadership
At St Matthew's, pupil leadership lies at the heart of our vision to let every child’s light shine. We believe that when children are trusted with responsibility, they grow in confidence, character and compassion - living out our school values in meaningful, real-world ways each day.
Our pupil leaders play a vital role in shaping a positive, inclusive and forward-thinking school community. Through our core roles of Rights Respecting Ambassadors, House Captains and the Eco Council, children develop the skills to lead with integrity, serve others and make a lasting difference.
Together, these roles provide opportunities for all of our pupils to actively contribute to school life, influence positive change and develop leadership skills that will serve them well beyond the classroom. Through pupil leadership, our children are not only prepared for the future – they are already helping to shape it!

pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
The Government believes that the Pupil Premium, which is additional to main school funding, is the best way to address the current underlying inequalities between children eligible for free school meals and their peers by ensuring that funding to tackle disadvantage reaches the pupils who need it most.
At our school, we are committed to ensuring that every child achieves their full potential, regardless of their background or starting point. The Pupil Premium is additional funding provided by the government to support pupils who may face barriers to learning, including those who are eligible for free school meals, have been eligible in the past, or are looked after by the local authority. Schools also receive funding for children who have been looked after continuously for more than six months, and children of service personnel. (DFE Website)
We carefully use this funding to provide targeted support, high-quality teaching, and enrichment opportunities that help all pupils succeed both academically and personally. Our approach focusses on removing barriers to learning, promoting inclusion, and raising aspirations for every child.

We regularly review the impact of our pupil premium spending to ensure it is making a meaningful difference to pupils’ progress and attainment. We are proud of our inclusive ethos and our commitment to enabling every child to flourish.
For further details, please see our Pupil Premium Strategy Statement below.
Our next pupil Premium Strategy will be published in December 2026.
